explanation.en: إِذَا is an adverb of future time carrying conditional meaning ("when/whenever"): ظرف لما يستقبل من الزمان متضمن معنى الشرط. Unlike إِنْ, it does not put verbs in jazm in standard prose — its verb is usually a past form understood as future: إِذَا دَخَلْتَ الْبَصْرَةَ (when you enter Basra). When the answer clause is a future statement, request, or nominal sentence, it is introduced by ف: فَسَيَأْتِيكَ النَّاسُ. Ibn Hisham treats إذا at length in Qatr al-Nada.

examples.en: When you enter Basra, the people will come to you.
When Allah's help and the victory come… (Quran 110:1)

why.en: Treating إذا like إنْ and jazming the verb. In prose إذا does not govern jazm; it prefers a past-tense verb with future meaning.
When the answer clause starts with س/سوف (or is a command or nominal sentence), it must be tied with the answer ف.
